newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish govt seen as losing battle on crime - poll.
newsitem.headline: Irish govt seen as losing battle on crime - poll.

text.p: A majority of people in Ireland believe their government is losing the battle to reduce crime, an Irish Times/MRBI poll said on Monday.

More than four out of five people (86 percent) believe crime is increasing and more than one third (36 percent) thought opposition party Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrat party would be more effective in handling crime, the poll showed.
Just 21 percent believed the policies of the current three-party coalition, Fine Gael, Labour and Democratic Left were most effective.

The findings contrast with an opinion poll published on Saturday showing satisfaction in the Irish government had increased to the highest level since it came to office in November 1994 when the previous coalition collapsed.

Saturday's survey put the satisfaction rating at 50 percent, up 11 points from six weeks ago, following last month's giveaway annual budget in which the standard rate of income tax was cut for the first time in five years.

The latest poll shows the public rates crime second to unemployment among the key issues in the run-up to the next general election, which must be held by November but is more likely to be called before June.
Polling was conducted among 1,000 electors at 100 sampling points throughout the state last week.
